name: Camera Follow
description: Owns the view: where the world is drawn from, and the only transform applied to it. It follows a target within a deadzone rather than centring on it exactly, because a camera pinned to a walking character makes the whole world jitter under every step, and smooths what is left so a jump does not snap the view. It also composes screen shake into the same matrix, since a shake is a camera effect and two components cannot each own the transform — presentation.screen_shake publishes an offset and a roll, and yields the view when a camera is present. The target is read optionally rather than declared as a dependency, so the same camera follows a side-view body or a top-down walker without either being required.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: deadzoneWidth
inputs.description: How far the target may move horizontally before the camera starts following, in world units. Zero pins the camera to the target and makes every footstep move the world.

inputs.name: deadzoneHeight
inputs.description: The vertical equivalent. Usually larger than it looks it should be: a jump is a big vertical excursion that the player does not want the camera to chase.

inputs.name: smoothingSeconds
inputs.description: Roughly how long the camera takes to close the gap once the target leaves the deadzone. 0 follows rigidly; large values read as the camera losing track.

inputs.name: clampToWorldBounds
inputs.description: Whether the view is kept inside the world rectangle, so the edge of the level is never on screen. Turn it off for a world with no meaningful edge.

inputs.name: zoom
inputs.description: Scale applied to the view. Above 1 shows less of the world and makes the camera's work visible even in a level that would otherwise fit on one screen.

outputs.name: center
outputs.description: The point the view is centred on, in world units.

outputs.name: ownsViewTransform
outputs.description: Always true while this component is in the build. Anything that would otherwise set its own view transform reads this and yields, so the view has exactly one owner.
